newsitem.title: USA: Ill. House sends $659 mln bond bill to governor.
newsitem.headline: Ill. House sends $659 mln bond bill to governor.

text.p: The Illinois House on Wednesday approved a $659 million general obligation bond authorization bill that had eluded passage for two years.
The bill, which was passed on a 106 to 4 vote and which passed the Senate earlier this month, now heads to the desk of Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar.
The bill's passage followed an agreement last week between Edgar and legislative leaders over the measure, which had been opposed by House Democrats during the previous two legislative sessions.

However, Edgar last week said that Moody's Investors Service's upgrade of the state's rating on Feb. 10 helped sway House Speaker Michael Madigan, D-Chicago, in addition to convincing Madigan that the money was needed for emergency prison, higher education and other projects.
The bill allows for $500 million of the GO bonds to be sold as college savings bonds.
A comment was not immediately available from Edgar's press office as to when the governor would sign the bond bill into law.
